marks.gloss_en: טעמא דאיכא תרי -- from Shmuel's 'there remain two' it follows that without two it is not kosher
the reason is that two remain; were two not to remain -- no [not kosher]
[in the איכא דאמרי version, Shmuel's reply] supports Rabbenai, who said in Shmuel's name: even as a sarbal thread -- kosher
what is its majority? the majority of each and every one
Mar bar Rav Ashi: once they are translucent -- even though they are not white
there are three strands, one thick and two thin
in birds there are sixteen strands
Rav: the tzomet of which they spoke -- [it is] by its majority
אנא עובדא ידענא -- R' Yochanan himself declared fit a fledgling where skin combined with flesh
בר גוזלא קאמרת? בר גוזלא דרכיך שאני -- a fledgling, which is soft, is different (= p_bar_gozala_rachich_shani)
אנא עובדא ידענא -- R' Yochanan declared fit a fledgling where skin combined with flesh (= p_ry_akhsher_bar_gozala; Rav Nachman's rejoinder is on s_ovada_bar_gozala)
a fledgling in R' Yitzchak's house, where skin combined with flesh, came before R' Yochanan and he declared it fit
חדא, דאמר רבי יוחנן: גידין שסופן להקשות נמנין עליהן בפסח
soft sinews [covering the break] came before Rabba; Rabba: what is there to be concerned about with them? -- permitted
מתקיף לה רב נחמן לשמואל: יאמרו אבר ממנה מוטל באשפה ומותרת? -- (as he clarifies at 76b.11: a limb from which it lives)
לרב נמי יאמרו אבר ממנה מוטל באשפה ומותרת! -- Rav too permits the animal and forbids the limb below the knee
Rav Nachman, as first phrased: people will say 'a limb of it lies on the dunghill and it is permitted?'
הכי קאמינא: אבר שחיה ממנה מוטל באשפה ומותרת? (= p_rn_yomru_ever_shechaya)
Rav Nachman, as he meant it: people will say 'a limb from which it lives lies on the dunghill and it is permitted?'

מתיב רב חסדא: לא, אם טיהרה שחיטת טרפה אותה ואת האבר המדולדל בה... -- the slaughter purifies the hanging limb, so it does not impart impurity by carrying (Rabba grades this source as a mere pircha: הדורי אפירכי למה לך)

No: if the slaughter of a tereifa purifies it and the limb hanging from it -- a thing of its own body -- shall it purify the fetus, a thing not of its body? (conceding that slaughter purifies the hanging limb)
אותיב ממתניתין: נשחטה בהמה -- הוכשרו בדמיה... -- the hanging limb is treated as food rendered susceptible, not as a limb that imparts impurity
the mishna: [hanging limb and flesh,] the animal was slaughtered -- they were rendered susceptible by its blood, the words of R' Meir; R' Shimon says: they were not
מתניתין איכא לדחויי, כדדחינן -- the mishna can be deflected, as we deflected it [elsewhere]
והא מיפלג פליג! -- but Shmuel disputes Rav
הדר ביה שמואל לגביה דרב (= p_hadar_bei_shmuel)
R' Zeira: and so Aryokh interpreted it in Babylonia
ולימא מר עור מצרף לבשר, דהא עור ובשר קתני! -- the baraita's 'skin and flesh' implies skin only combines
אנן עור או בשר תנינן -- we learn [the baraita as] 'skin OR flesh'
R' Yochanan (via Ulla): skin is like flesh
ולימא מר עור משלים לבשר לחומרא! -- let the master say [only] that skin completes flesh, stringently
R' Yochanan (via Ulla, in the איכא דאמרי version): skin combines with flesh
broken above the knee joint, the majority of the flesh intact: both [animal and limb] are permitted
Shmuel: whether above or below, if not [intact]: the limb is forbidden and the animal permitted -- so above the knee too
the halakha follows Rav [on the break above the knee]
the baraita: a bone broke and protruded -- if skin and flesh cover its majority, it is permitted
